requirements.quote:
A 1-RTT packet uses a short packet header.  It is used after the
   version and 1-RTT keys are negotiated.
requirements.condition: When sending or processing a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Use the short packet header, and use the packet only after the version and 1-RTT keys have been negotiated.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a 1-RTT packet before the version and 1-RTT keys have been negotiated.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-header form and the negotiation state at the time of 1-RTT packet use can be observed in implementation state and packet traces.

requirements.quote:
1-RTT Packet {
     Header Form (1) = 0,
     Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
     Spin Bit (1),
     Reserved Bits (2),
     Key Phase (1),
     Packet Number Length (2),
     Destination Connection ID (0..160),
     Packet Number (8..32),
     Packet Payload (8..),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Use the displayed field order: Header Form, Fixed Bit, Spin Bit, Reserved Bits, Key Phase, Packet Number Length, Destination Connection ID, Packet Number, and Packet Payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode these 1-RTT packet fields in a different order.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet parser or serialized packet can be inspected to verify the field sequence.

requirements.quote:
1-RTT Packet {
     Header Form (1) = 0,
     Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
     Spin Bit (1),
     Reserved Bits (2),
     Key Phase (1),
     Packet Number Length (2),
     Destination Connection ID (0..160),
     Packet Number (8..32),
     Packet Payload (8..),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Header Form as one bit with value 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode a nonzero Header Form bit.
requirements.why_checkable: The width and fixed value can be checked directly in the serialized first byte.

requirements.quote:
1-RTT Packet {
     Header Form (1) = 0,
     Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
     Spin Bit (1),
     Reserved Bits (2),
     Key Phase (1),
     Packet Number Length (2),
     Destination Connection ID (0..160),
     Packet Number (8..32),
     Packet Payload (8..),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Fixed Bit as one bit with value 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode a zero Fixed Bit.
requirements.why_checkable: The width and fixed value can be checked directly in the serialized first byte.

requirements.quote:
1-RTT Packet {
     Header Form (1) = 0,
     Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
     Spin Bit (1),
     Reserved Bits (2),
     Key Phase (1),
     Packet Number Length (2),
     Destination Connection ID (0..160),
     Packet Number (8..32),
     Packet Payload (8..),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Allocate 1 bit to Spin Bit, 2 bits to Reserved Bits, 1 bit to Key Phase, and 2 bits to Packet Number Length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use different widths for these fields.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit-field layout can be verified in encoder and parser logic or serialized packets.

requirements.quote:
1-RTT Packet {
     Header Form (1) = 0,
     Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
     Spin Bit (1),
     Reserved Bits (2),
     Key Phase (1),
     Packet Number Length (2),
     Destination Connection ID (0..160),
     Packet Number (8..32),
     Packet Payload (8..),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Use a Destination Connection ID whose length is between 0 and 160 bits inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a Destination Connection ID longer than 160 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Destination Connection ID length can be measured.

requirements.quote:
1-RTT Packet {
     Header Form (1) = 0,
     Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
     Spin Bit (1),
     Reserved Bits (2),
     Key Phase (1),
     Packet Number Length (2),
     Destination Connection ID (0..160),
     Packet Number (8..32),
     Packet Payload (8..),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Use a Packet Number field whose length is between 8 and 32 bits inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a Packet Number field shorter than 8 bits or longer than 32 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Packet Number field length can be measured.

requirements.quote:
1-RTT Packet {
     Header Form (1) = 0,
     Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
     Spin Bit (1),
     Reserved Bits (2),
     Key Phase (1),
     Packet Number Length (2),
     Destination Connection ID (0..160),
     Packet Number (8..32),
     Packet Payload (8..),
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Packet Payload of at least 8 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode an empty Packet Payload or one shorter than 8 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Payload presence and encoded length can be measured in a packet.

requirements.quote:
Header Form:  The most significant bit (0x80) of byte 0 is set to 0
      for the short header.
requirements.condition: When encoding a short header
requirements.required_behavior: Set the most significant bit, masked by 0x80, of byte 0 to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Set the short-header Header Form bit to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit can be inspected directly in byte 0 of an encoded short header.

requirements.quote:
Fixed Bit:  The next bit (0x40) of byte 0 is set to 1.  Packets
      containing a zero value for this bit are not valid packets in this
      version and MUST be discarded.  A value of 1 for this bit allows
      QUIC to coexist with other protocols; see [RFC7983].
requirements.condition: When encoding a 1-RTT short header
requirements.required_behavior: Set the bit masked by 0x40 in byte 0 to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode the Fixed Bit as 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The Fixed Bit value is directly observable in the encoded first byte.

requirements.quote:
Fixed Bit:  The next bit (0x40) of byte 0 is set to 1.  Packets
      containing a zero value for this bit are not valid packets in this
      version and MUST be discarded.  A value of 1 for this bit allows
      QUIC to coexist with other protocols; see [RFC7983].
requirements.condition: When receiving a packet whose bit masked by 0x40 in byte 0 is zero
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept or continue processing the packet as a valid packet in this QUIC version.
requirements.why_checkable: A focused input packet with the bit cleared can verify that the receiver discards it.

requirements.quote:
Spin Bit:  The third most significant bit (0x20) of byte 0 is the
      latency spin bit, set as described in Section 17.4.
requirements.condition: When setting the latency spin bit
requirements.required_behavior: Set the bit according to Section 17.4.
requirements.why_checkable: The cited setting algorithm is not present in this chunk, so the required bit behavior cannot be determined from the supplied evidence alone.

requirements.quote:
Reserved Bits:  The next two bits (those with a mask of 0x18) of byte
      0 are reserved.  These bits are protected using header protection;
      see Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].  The value included prior to
      protection MUST be set to 0.  An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a
      packet that has a non-zero value for these bits, after removing
      both packet and header protection, as a connection error of type
      PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.  Discarding such a packet after only removing
      header protection can expose the endpoint to attacks; see
      Section 9.5 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: Before applying header protection to a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Set both reserved bits masked by 0x18 in byte 0 to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include a nonzero reserved-bit value prior to protection.
requirements.why_checkable: The pre-protection header value can be inspected in packet-construction logic or a focused encoder test.

requirements.quote:
Reserved Bits:  The next two bits (those with a mask of 0x18) of byte
      0 are reserved.  These bits are protected using header protection;
      see Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].  The value included prior to
      protection MUST be set to 0.  An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a
      packet that has a non-zero value for these bits, after removing
      both packet and header protection, as a connection error of type
      PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.  Discarding such a packet after only removing
      header protection can expose the endpoint to attacks; see
      Section 9.5 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When encoding a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the two reserved bits using header protection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Transmit the reserved bits without header protection.
requirements.why_checkable: The sender's protection transformation can be tested or inspected to confirm that the reserved bits participate in header protection.

requirements.quote:
Reserved Bits:  The next two bits (those with a mask of 0x18) of byte
      0 are reserved.  These bits are protected using header protection;
      see Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].  The value included prior to
      protection MUST be set to 0.  An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a
      packet that has a non-zero value for these bits, after removing
      both packet and header protection, as a connection error of type
      PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.  Discarding such a packet after only removing
      header protection can expose the endpoint to attacks; see
      Section 9.5 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: After both packet protection and header protection have been removed from a received packet, and its reserved bits are nonzero
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept the packet or treat the condition as a non-connection-level error.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A protected test packet that reveals nonzero reserved bits after both protections are removed can verify the resulting connection error and error type.

requirements.quote:
Reserved Bits:  The next two bits (those with a mask of 0x18) of byte
      0 are reserved.  These bits are protected using header protection;
      see Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].  The value included prior to
      protection MUST be set to 0.  An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a
      packet that has a non-zero value for these bits, after removing
      both packet and header protection, as a connection error of type
      PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.  Discarding such a packet after only removing
      header protection can expose the endpoint to attacks; see
      Section 9.5 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When checking a received packet for a nonzero reserved-bit violation
requirements.required_behavior: Remove both packet protection and header protection before determining and handling the reserved-bit violation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Discard the packet for this reserved-bit condition after removing only header protection.
requirements.why_checkable: The receiver's processing order can be instrumented to verify that packet protection is removed before the reserved-bit decision.

requirements.quote:
Key Phase:  The next bit (0x04) of byte 0 indicates the key phase,
      which allows a recipient of a packet to identify the packet
      protection keys that are used to protect the packet.  See
      [QUIC-TLS] for details.  This bit is protected using header
      protection; see Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When encoding a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Use the bit masked by 0x04 in byte 0 as the Key Phase bit and protect it using header protection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Transmit the Key Phase bit without header protection.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit position and its participation in header protection can be verified in encoder logic and packet transformations.

requirements.quote:
Packet Number Length:  The least significant two bits (those with a
      mask of 0x03) of byte 0 contain the length of the Packet Number
      field, encoded as an unsigned two-bit integer that is one less
      than the length of the Packet Number field in bytes.  That is, the
      length of the Packet Number field is the value of this field plus
      one.  These bits are protected using header protection; see
      Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Packet Number Length field
requirements.required_behavior: Use the least significant two bits, masked by 0x03, of byte 0 and encode the unsigned value as the Packet Number length in bytes minus one; equivalently, derive the byte length as the field value plus one.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode the direct byte length or derive a length other than the field value plus one.
requirements.why_checkable: All four field values can be tested against their corresponding Packet Number lengths of one through four bytes.

requirements.quote:
Packet Number Length:  The least significant two bits (those with a
      mask of 0x03) of byte 0 contain the length of the Packet Number
      field, encoded as an unsigned two-bit integer that is one less
      than the length of the Packet Number field in bytes.  That is, the
      length of the Packet Number field is the value of this field plus
      one.  These bits are protected using header protection; see
      Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When encoding a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the Packet Number Length bits using header protection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Transmit the Packet Number Length bits without header protection.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet transformations can verify that the two length bits participate in header protection.

requirements.quote:
Destination Connection ID:  The Destination Connection ID is a
      connection ID that is chosen by the intended recipient of the
      packet.  See Section 5.1 for more details.
requirements.condition: When selecting the Destination Connection ID for a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Use a connection ID chosen by the packet's intended recipient.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a connection ID not chosen by the intended recipient.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Destination Connection ID can be compared with the connection IDs issued or selected by the intended recipient.

requirements.quote:
Packet Number:  The Packet Number field is 1 to 4 bytes long.  The
      packet number is protected using header protection; see
      Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].  The length of the Packet Number field
      is encoded in Packet Number Length field.  See Section 17.1 for
      details.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a 1-RTT Packet Number field
requirements.required_behavior: Use a Packet Number field length from 1 through 4 bytes inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a Packet Number field shorter than 1 byte or longer than 4 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized Packet Number field length can be measured directly.

requirements.quote:
Packet Number:  The Packet Number field is 1 to 4 bytes long.  The
      packet number is protected using header protection; see
      Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].  The length of the Packet Number field
      is encoded in Packet Number Length field.  See Section 17.1 for
      details.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and obtain the Packet Number field length from the Packet Number Length field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a Packet Number field length inconsistent with the Packet Number Length field.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared length value can be compared with the actual number of Packet Number bytes.

requirements.quote:
Packet Number:  The Packet Number field is 1 to 4 bytes long.  The
      packet number is protected using header protection; see
      Section 5.4 of [QUIC-TLS].  The length of the Packet Number field
      is encoded in Packet Number Length field.  See Section 17.1 for
      details.
requirements.condition: When encoding a 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the packet number using header protection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Transmit the packet number without header protection.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet transformations can verify that the Packet Number field participates in header protection.

requirements.quote:
Packet Payload:  1-RTT packets always include a 1-RTT protected
      payload.
requirements.condition: For every 1-RTT packet
requirements.required_behavior: Include a 1-RTT protected payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit the payload or include it without 1-RTT protection.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized packets and sender logic can be checked for payload presence and application of 1-RTT protection.

requirements.quote:
The header form bit and the Destination Connection ID field of a
   short header packet are version independent.  The remaining fields
   are specific to the selected QUIC version.  See [QUIC-INVARIANTS] for
   details on how packets from different versions of QUIC are
   interpreted.
requirements.condition: When interpreting a short header packet across QUIC versions
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the Header Form bit and Destination Connection ID as version-independent, and interpret all remaining fields according to the selected QUIC version.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply selected-version-specific interpretation to the Header Form bit or Destination Connection ID, or treat the remaining fields as version-independent.
requirements.why_checkable: Version-dispatch and parser logic can be inspected or tested across selected versions to verify which fields use invariant versus version-specific interpretation.
